source_text:
Οἱ γὰρ ἀμφὶ τὸν
Συμεῶνα καὶ τὸν Λευῒ, οὐ μετρίως ἀπογευσάμενοι τῆς ἀνδροφονίας, ἐν συνηθείᾳ μὲν ἤδη ποτὲ τοῦ πράγματος ἐγεγόνεισαν, ἕρπειν δὲ περὶ τὰς τοιαύτας ὠρέγοντο κνίσας
thought_title: Simeon and Levi's taste for murder
orientation: Eustathius is contrasting Joseph's self-control with the violent habits of his brothers Simeon and Levi.
pass_a_gloss: For those around Simeon and Levi, having tasted murder not moderately, had already at some time come to be in a habit of the deed, and they desired to creep around such savory smells.

choices.term: οἱ ἀμφὶ τὸν Συμεῶνα καὶ τὸν Λευΐ
choices.why: The phrase 'οἱ ἀμφὶ' can mean 'the followers of' or 'the party of,' but here it likely refers to Simeon and Levi themselves and their associates; rendering literally as 'those around' preserves the Greek idiom without overinterpreting.
rejected: the company of Simeon and Levi

choices.why: The litotes 'not moderately' is kept literal to preserve the understatement and the force of the Greek adverb.

choices.term: ἐν συνηθείᾳ μὲν ἤδη ποτὲ τοῦ πράγματος ἐγεγόνεισαν
choices.english: had already at some time come to be in a habit of the deed
choices.why: The pluperfect 'ἐγεγόνεισαν' with 'ἐν συνηθείᾳ' is rendered literally to show the completed state of habituation; 'ἤδη ποτέ' is kept as 'already at some time' to preserve the temporal nuance.
rejected: had already become accustomed to the deed
were already in the habit of the deed

choices.term: ἕρπειν δὲ περὶ τὰς τοιαύτας ὠρέγοντο κνίσας
choices.english: and they desired to creep around such savory smells
choices.why: The metaphor of creeping around savory smells (κνίσας) is vivid and unusual; keeping it literal preserves the sensory image of being drawn to the scent of murder.
rejected: and they longed to crawl toward such odors
and they craved to slink around such fumes

pass_b_english: For Simeon and Levi and their company had tasted murder in no small measure, and by now they had made a settled habit of the deed; they even longed to go creeping around the scent of blood.

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'murder' for ἀνδροφονία; 'savory smells' obscures the metaphor's referent to murder.
last_rejected.fix: they even longed to go creeping around such scents of murder
last_rejected.ruling: κνίσας correctly rendered as 'savory smells'; glossary issue is spurious since ἀνδροφονίας is already translated 'murder'.

last_rejected.why: κνίσας means 'sacrificial smoke/smell' but metaphorically refers back to murder, not literal food smells.
last_rejected.ruling: κνίσας means savory smell of roasting meat; 'savory smells' captures the word and metaphor without needing explicit glossing.

problems.quote: they even longed to go creeping around such savory smells
problems.why: Odd metaphor for murder; likely a hunting/blood-scent image mistranslated as food.
problems.fix: Render as 'the scent of blood' or similar hunting imagery.

edits.old: they even longed to go creeping around such savory smells
edits.new: they even longed to go creeping around the scent of blood
